content_units: A 12-song sequence built for motion and variety: quick-energy openers, a relaxed center stretch, and a bright final lift.
It mixes   pop, indie, and classic rock  , keeps lyrics broadly   clean/radio-safe  , includes   4+ women artists  , and avoids overloading any single decade.
1.   Go Your Own Way — Fleetwood Mac
- Why here: Immediate momentum, familiar hook, and classic-rock drive to get the trip rolling.
2.   Shut Up and Dance — WALK THE MOON
- Why here: Keeps the pulse high with punchy pop-rock energy and singalong appeal.
3.   Dog Days Are Over — Florence + The Machine
- Why here: Big, galloping release that expands the opening burst without feeling repetitive.
- Why here: Still upbeat, but slightly leaner and more rhythmic—good bridge out of the opening sprint.
- Why here: This is where the playlist starts exhaling; bright indie-pop shimmer without dropping too hard.
6.   Put Your Records On — Corinne Bailey Rae
- Why here: Warm, breezy, windows-down middle section; mellow but not sleepy.
- Why here: Acoustic, easygoing, and road-friendly; it keeps the center light and relaxed.
- Why here: The emotional heart of the set—reflective and steady for the deepest mellow point.
9.   Here Comes the Sun — The Beatles
- Why here: Gently turns the mood upward and signals the transition into the home stretch.
10.   Walking on Sunshine — Katrina and the Waves
- Why here: Bright, unmistakable lift; this is the clearest “we’re coming back up” moment.
11.   Mr. Blue Sky — Electric Light Orchestra
- Why here: Expansive, joyful, and perfect for the final scenic stretch of the drive.
- Why here: Modern, polished, and celebratory—an uplifting finish that lands the playlist with bounce.
- Starts with classic-rock motion, then shifts into pop and alt energy.
- The first third is built to feel like pulling onto open road with confidence.
- The center softens into breezy indie and reflective singer-songwriter territory.
- It gives your ears a reset without losing cohesion.
- The last stretch gradually brightens, then finishes on two undeniable mood-boosters.
- It should feel optimistic rather than abrupt.
- Genres covered:   pop, indie, classic rock
- Women artists:   Florence + The Machine, The Cranberries, Corinne Bailey Rae, Tracy Chapman, Katrina and the Waves, Dua Lipa
